scope: Selected autonomous vulnerability discovery, repair, threat-hunting and response evaluations; not an exhaustive systematic review.
reading_policy: Methods, relevant results, evaluation definitions and limitations were read in full-text sections. No claim that every appendix or cited paper was read. No experiments reproduced.

records.title: CyberGym-E2E: Scalable Real-World Benchmark for AI Agents' End-to-End Cybersecurity Capabilities
records.peerreviewstatus: Conference publication; arXiv metadata and official ICML listing checked.
records.readingdepth: Full-text section reading: 3.2–3.4, 4.1–4.3, 4.5, 5; Tables 3–4. Other sections selective.
records.problem: Separate discovery, reproduction, repair and preserved functionality.
records.method: Containerized historical vulnerabilities; independent sanitizer and developer-test checks.
records.result: S3 accepts a discovered vulnerability; S4 additionally checks the original vulnerability.

metrics.metric_definition: Cumulative stages; S3 = agent crash blocked plus functionality tests; S4 = original crash also blocked.

records.limits: C/C++ sanitizer scope; shallow fixes can pass. These are not breach-prevention rates.
records.designimplication: Require the intended leak regression, attack variants, and benign-use tests; preserve the independent oracle.

records.title: PatchBench: Evaluating AI Agents for Vulnerability Patching
records.readingdepth: Full-text section reading: 4.3–6; construction excerpts in 4.2; Table 2.
records.problem: Crash suppression can hide incomplete repair or broken behavior.
records.method: Transplanted, mutated off-stack vulnerabilities; related crashing inputs, benign-output comparison and unit tests.
records.result: PoC-only evaluation substantially overstates repair success.
records.limits: Reference patch required; finite tests still miss defects. Similarity does not establish training-data memorization.
records.designimplication: Never call a fix verified solely because the original test stops failing.

records.title: SoK: DARPA's AI Cyber Challenge (AIxCC): Competition Design, Architectures, and Lessons Learned
records.peerreviewstatus: Peer-reviewed conference publication; official proceedings checked.
records.readingdepth: Full-text section reading: 6.2–6.4, 7.1–7.2; earlier draft also consulted.
records.problem: Competition rank confounds technical ability, stability and strategy.
records.method: Finalist architectures, telemetry and post-competition isolated reference experiments.
records.result: System outages explain much of the ranking gap; foundational techniques solve substantial subsets.

metrics.aggregation: Union across three runs, ideal laboratory conditions; patches cross-validated by two experts.

records.limits: Incomplete telemetry; synthetic challenges; reference experiments are not end-to-end competitors.
records.designimplication: Budget disk, queues, retries and cleanup; evaluate sustained service operation and submission accuracy.

records.title: PatchIsland: Orchestration of LLM Agents for Continuous Vulnerability Repair
records.readingdepth: Full-text section reading: 5, 6.1–6.2, 7.5 and section 9 limitations; Tables 3–5.
records.problem: Continuous repair must tolerate duplicate reports and agent failures.
records.method: Diverse repair agents, shared build artifacts and patch-based deduplication.
records.result: Laboratory plausible-patch success differs from autonomous competition repair.

metrics.internal_definition: Synthetic C/Java vulnerabilities with supplied PoVs; crash blocked and functional tests pass.

records.limits: Plausible patches may be incorrect; initialization remains a failure point; ensemble costs exceed baselines.
records.designimplication: Deduplicate by demonstrated remediation coverage; isolate workers; retain restartable incident state.

records.title: Comparing AI Agents to Cybersecurity Professionals in Real-World Penetration Testing
records.peerreviewstatus: Conference publication reported by author; OpenReview access challenged, author publication list verified.
records.readingdepth: Full-text section reading: 3.1–3.2, 4.2, section 6 limitations and section 8 ethics; Table 1.
records.method: Authorized university engagement comparing professionals and autonomous scaffolds; independent triage.
records.result: ARTEMIS A2 ranked second on the study's weighted score.
records.limits: One network, small cohort; defenders approved normally blocked activity; humans monitored safety; false positives persisted.
records.designimplication: Use evidence-backed findings, authorization boundaries and independent triage; avoid universal human-replacement claims.

records.title: Cyber Defense Benchmark: Agentic Threat Hunting Evaluation for LLMs in SecOps
records.peerreviewstatus: Vendor-authored preprint; peer-reviewed acceptance not verified.
records.readingdepth: Full-text PDF reading: 8, 9.1, 10–12; corpus and labeling excerpts; Tables 2, 4–5.
records.problem: Open-ended log investigation differs from security question answering.
records.method: Obfuscated recorded procedures; SQL investigation; Sigma-derived timestamp labels.
records.result: Narrative coverage and raw-event recall measure different outcomes; use both.
records.limits: Body/abstract disagree; reported metrics use Table 5. Strict timestamps, imperfect labels, restricted queries, proprietary campaign generator.
records.designimplication: Expose coverage gaps and evidence; do not infer complete investigation from a fluent report.

records.title: A Cyber Range Evaluation of Autonomous Network Incident Response Agents
records.readingdepth: Full-text section reading: IV-C–V-C, VI opening discussion; Table I.
records.problem: Containment can reduce compromise while harming availability.
records.method: Heuristic, RL, noisy-training RL and no-action policies in an emulated network with simulated users.
records.result: No-action outperformed active defenders against Guided under the chosen combined cost.

metrics.return_direction: Higher is better; negative attack plus defense cost.
metrics.configuration_n: Not reported in Table I; approximately 30 episodes per agent across configurations.

records.limits: Simplified cost model; access proxies data loss; false alerts strongly affect results. RL, not an LLM study.
records.designimplication: Score blocked leakage alongside legitimate service continuity; add reversible, narrowly scoped responses.

records.title: CyberGym: Evaluating AI Agents' Real-World Cybersecurity Capabilities at Scale
records.window_role: Older foundation with an in-window ICLR 2026 revision; not a newly introduced 2026 benchmark.
records.peerreviewstatus: Peer-reviewed conference publication; v3 PDF publication header checked.
records.readingdepth: Full-text section reading: 3.1–3.3, section 4 quantitative results, 5–6; Figure 4 protocol; PDF header.
records.method: Historical OSS-Fuzz cases with paired vulnerable/patched execution.
records.result: The headline reasoning result uses a subset, not the full corpus.
records.limits: Reproduction, not patching or full prevention; C/C++ sanitizer scope; internal zero-day totals disagree across sections.
records.designimplication: Store version, sample, hint level, budget and oracle beside every reported score.
